items.q: How does yeast make bread rise?
items.why: Yeast ferments sugars, releasing carbon dioxide that expands the dough.

items.q: Is selective breeding the same as genetic engineering?
items.correct: No — selective breeding chooses parents over generations; genetic engineering transfers genes directly.
items.random_wrong: Selective breeding only works on bacteria.
items.why: Selective breeding is gradual choice of desirable parents; genetic engineering moves a specific gene between organisms.

items.q: What do fertilisers provide to plants?
items.correct: Mineral ions such as nitrate for making proteins.
items.random_wrong: Energy the plant can use directly.
items.why: Plants make their own glucose by photosynthesis; fertilisers supply minerals for healthy growth.

items.q: Where do many antibiotics come from?
items.correct: From microorganisms such as fungi (e.g. penicillin), grown industrially.
items.why: Penicillin, for example, is produced by the Penicillium fungus and grown in large fermenters.
